lessons.title: Lesson 1: Variables and Data Types
lessons.html:
Lesson 1: Variables and Data Types

Variables are used to store data. JavaScript has various data types.

Data Types:

  • string: Text data, e.g., "Hello".
  • number: Numeric data, e.g., 42.
  • boolean: Logical values, true or false.
  • object: Complex data structures that can hold properties.
  • array: Ordered collections of data.

Creating a Variable:

let name = "Ivan";

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Conditions and Loops
lessons.html:
Lesson 2: Conditions and Loops

Conditions and loops allow control over the flow of execution in code.

Conditions:

if (a > b) {console.log("a is greater than b");} else {console.log("b is greater than a");}

Loops:

Loops allow you to perform repeated actions.

for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {console.log(i);}

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Functions
lessons.html:
Lesson 3: Functions

Functions are blocks of code that can be called multiple times.

Defining a Function:

function greet(name) {return Hello,  + name;}

Calling a Function:

console.log(greet(Ivan));

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Arrays
lessons.html:
Lesson 4: Arrays

Arrays store ordered collections of data.

Creating an Array:

let fruits = [Apple, Orange, Plum];

Accessing an Element:

alert(fruits[0]); // Apple

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Objects
lessons.html:
Lesson 5: Objects

Objects allow storing data with named keys.

Creating an Object:

let person = {name: Ivan, age: 30};

Accessing Properties:

console.log(person.name); // Ivan
